Run a chat request

Ollama OpenAI-Compatible API

Use http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/ as the OpenAI SDK base URL and ollama as its placeholder API key for a standard local Ollama server. Pick an exact model ID from /v1/models. If chat returns 404, check whether the SDK reached /v1/chat/completions, then check the model tag in the response.

  1. Connect the OpenAI Python SDK
  2. Find the failing step
  3. Fix connection errors
  4. Distinguish two kinds of 404
  5. Download the tested responses

Connect the OpenAI Python SDK

Start Ollama and make sure at least one local model is present. If you need a model, follow the first local model guide. Use the actual port if it differs from 11434. From the same machine as Ollama, check the compatible models endpoint:

curl --noproxy '*' -fsS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/models

Copy a model ID from data[].id. Install openai in your Python environment if needed. Replace the example ID with the one you just copied.

from openai import OpenAI

with OpenAI(
    base_url="http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/",
    api_key="ollama",
    max_retries=0,
    timeout=45,
) as client:
    reply = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="qwen2.5:0.5b",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly LOCAL_OK."}],
        max_tokens=16,
        temperature=0,
    )
    print(reply.choices[0].message.content)

A short reply from the chosen model confirms the chat route works. The SDK appends chat/completions to its base URL. A client field labeled full endpoint may instead expect http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions. The 45-second diagnostic timeout may be too short for a larger model loading for the first time.

The placeholder satisfies the SDK’s key setting. Standard Ollama on loopback does not require authentication. A remote proxy or Ollama Cloud can have different authentication requirements. Use an actual provider key only with its intended service.

Fix connection errors before changing the API key

curl --noproxy '*' -fsS --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version

A version response confirms a server answered on that address. If the connection is refused, open the Ollama app or start ollama serve if you use the CLI and no instance is already listening. Recheck the address and port from the same environment as your client. In a container, 127.0.0.1 refers to that container. A connection timeout can have other causes, including an unreachable host or proxy configuration.

After the version response succeeds, retry /v1/models. If only the native API is answering, verify the exact compatible path and your Ollama version. For the OpenCode model picker, use the separate OpenCode and Ollama guide.

Distinguish two kinds of 404

  1. Wrong route. With the Python base URL set to the server root, our request went to /chat/completions and returned plain-text 404 page not found. Set the SDK base URL to the server address followed by /v1/, then check that the SDK calls /v1/chat/completions.
  2. Missing model. With the correct route and an unknown tag, our request returned a JSON error naming the missing model. List /v1/models again and copy an ID. The native /api/tags endpoint also lists models, using a different response format.

If a known ID still fails, check that the model list and chat go to the same host and port. Once a short request works, use the Ollama context guide if you need to verify the loaded context for a longer task.

What the local requests returned

On November 28, 2026 we used one small Qwen GGUF, Ollama 0.40.18 and the OpenAI Python SDK on a temporary loopback port. The SDK chat and a direct HTTP request with no Authorization header both returned LOCAL_OK. The native and compatible model lists showed the same tag. The two deliberate 404s had different paths and bodies. After stopping Ollama, the SDK raised APIConnectionError.

Download the model lists, request and observed responses. The test covers local Chat Completions with one installed model. Other compatible endpoints and remote authentication depend on the version and deployment.
